steps.cap: An AI chip does all its work with transistors, tiny switches built into the silicon. One Nvidia Blackwell GPU holds 208 billion of them. Making the switches is the front end of the factory, and wiring them together comes after.
Each one is a switch. Seen end on, current flows through a strip of silicon, the channel, and the gate sits on top.
Switching off, the gate squeezes the flow shut, but only near itself. In a tiny transistor, current still leaks through the part it cannot reach.
Stand the channel on edge as a fin, and the gate covers three sides. Much less gets through.
Split it into thin sheets and wrap the gate around every side, and it shuts far tighter. That lets the switches keep shrinking, so each new chip can pack in more of them.
